short_description: Consumer-facing personality trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal for neuroticism-related emotional reactivity tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing personality trait with strong raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited emotional reactivity tendency and current mood or mental-health state for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with neuroticism-related emotional reactivity tendency, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Neuroticism tendency is presented here as a cautious relative personality signal linked to emotional sensitivity and stress reactivity, not as a diagnosis of anxiety, depression, or any other mental-health condition. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result, a mental-health diagnosis, or a direct readout of current mood.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.

Neuroticism is a broad research personality construct rather than a clinical diagnosis, and real-world emotional experience is influenced strongly by life events, stress load, sleep, relationships, culture, and measurement method.

The source score contains many variants, so raw-array overlap can remain modest in percentage terms even when matched-variant counts are large; interpret this as a cautious comparative signal, not as a precise personality measurement.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
